Incident Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT fired: reserved_pool_high_latency for tenant=greenfield. p95=1250ms (>1000ms), error_rate=2.4%. Triggered by metric-rule reserved_pool.p95_latency. PagerDuty incident PD-4821 created and auto-paged.

PagerDuty: Auto-page to oncall rotation; escalation policy: dedicated-reserved-high-latency.

Maya (oncall): Acked PD-4821. I'm taking ownership — will coordinate mitigation. Paging @TJ and @Carol. Any early signs of a config push?

TJ (sre): Looking now — no recent deploys to greenfield cluster in last 30m. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/dashboard/d/greenfield/reserved-pool (p95 and queue depth). Seeing concurrent increase in queue length and socket timeouts. Node CPU ~92%, GPU util steady.

Carol (infra): Confirmed high infra contention on reserved pool "greenfield-reserved-02". Autoscaler didn't kick due to scale lock (manual override) set earlier this week. I'm removing the lock and triggering a manual scale.

Maya (oncall): Good catch. Can we get +2 nodes immediately and enable temporary burst capacity? Also open a customer-impact note: greenfield team may see degraded latency and occasional 502/503  — mark SEV-2 until stabilized.

Carol (infra): Running command to scale now:
```
# redwoodctl (dedicated control plane)
redwoodctl reserved scale --tenant greenfield --add-nodes 2 --reason "p95 spike automated page"
```
Response: scaling started, nodes provisioning (ETA ~2m).

TJ (sre): While nodes come up, suggest immediate traffic soft-failover to fallback model variant to reduce per-request exec time. Updating routing policy for tenant.

Maya (oncall): Which variant? We should prefer a quantized/fast model — acceptance: reduce p95 by >=50% or fallback to queued throttle that returns early failure.

TJ (sre): Rolling routing change: set tenant routing policy to prefer model "rwd-mini-quant-v1" with fallback. Command:
```
# update routing via api
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.redwood/api/v1/tenants/greenfield/routing" -H "Authorization: Bearer $RO_API_TOKEN" -d '{"preferred_model":"rwd-mini-quant-v1","fallback":"gpt-lite-quant"}'
```
Applied. Starting warmup of KV cache for the variant.

Maya (oncall): Noted. Also lowering cache TTLs and enabling prefix caching for common prompts — should reduce kv-miss penalty.

Incident Bot: PD update: PD-4821 acknowledged by Maya (oncall) at 11:02:12 UTC. Escalation paused.

Carol (infra): New nodes joined reserved pool, autoscaler lock removed. Current pool size +2 (effective). Observability: CPU dropped to 68% across pool, queue depth falling.

TJ (sre): After routing change and scale: p95 trending down: 1,250ms -> 280ms -> 120ms over ~8m. Error rate back to 0.3%. Still monitoring for tail latency.

Maya (oncall): Customer impact update posted to #customer-impact (greenfield): short-term latency spike, mitigations applied (scale + routing fallback). Logging: minimal request loss; asked CS to expect a few support tickets.

Carol (infra): Follow-up ops action: re-enable autoscaler with relaxed cooldown and remove manual overrides. Command executed. Also flagged nodes for postmortem: why lock persisted.

TJ (sre): Runbook note: we hit a site-protection threshold due to manual scale lock. Action item to add runbook check to the scale lock flow (alert if lock present during autoscaler windup).

Maya (oncall): Handing continuous monitoring to TJ for the next two hours. I'll stay on thread for customer comms. If metrics stay stable for 30m, we'll resolve PD and mark incident as mitigated.

PagerDuty: PD-4821: Status -> Investigating -> Mitigated (pending final verification).

TJ (sre): 30m check-in: p95 = 110ms, error_rate = 0.08%, queue_depth normalized. Looks stable. No further action required immediate. Will run a quick stress test to validate autoscaler behavior.

Maya (oncall): Thanks all. Closing PD after 45m of stable metrics. Initial root-cause hypothesis: manual scale lock prevented autoscaler from reacting to a short QPS surge; combined with routing heat on a hot prefix, causing KV cache churn.

Carol (infra): Created follow-up ticket INFRA-1124: investigate scale lock UI/automation. Assigned to infra eng, priority P2.

Maya (oncall): Postmortem owners: Maya (incident lead), TJ (technical lead), Carol (infra lead). ETA for draft: 3 business days.

Incident Bot: PD-4821 closed at 11:50:03 UTC. :white_check_mark:

Maya (oncall): Final note: if anyone sees recurring p95 blips for greenfield, ping me directly. Thanks for the quick responses :thumbsup:
